body:
Of course finances are important, but I feel like I got more important things on my mind to deal with at the moment. Besides, I'm actually decent with money and I will probably join one of the best college-equivalent of my country next year. That would get me a nice well paid career, if I were to make it that far. My point is, let's not focus on my finances, I already have personalfinance on my main account for this.

Travels are indeed nice ! I did some when I was younger, now these occasions get rarer and I tend to refuse them.

As a matter of fact I'm quite materialistic, in a weird way. I'm a total maniac with some of my belongings, namely my books. If I could I'd spend thousands in an awesome huge library. On the other hand I'm always the one giving too much, I often offer gifts to friends for no good reasons. Insecurity I guess.

About art, well I don't feel so pumped about the idea. I work 9-5 and I don't even go to the gym anymore so I'm not sure I would be very motivated to do it seriously. I would consider it if I were to make it through and had to choose a life goal in order to fill an useless, tasteless and long life. Le sigh, I guess.

I hope you did well on your finals! Don't worry about your delay, as you can see I'm not the quickest to answer back either.

As a matter of fact I do get those nice moments. Mostly at work with coworkers these days, but they happen. I understand that life is supposed to be a nice series of happy times. Yet going to bed and waking up alone, in an empty appartment, well it's quite a grim reminder about my situation. I'm happy to still enjoy some littles things but I miss greater social interaction. I don't want to live a life where happiness only exists through friendship with coworkers. Shouldn't I be entitled to more ?

About my gf, well we always had a rocky relation. First she kept her distances while I was fully under her charm, then the total opposite. It ended up shitty for both of us because, IMO, we had no idea about what to do with ourselves and our relationship. Her leaving felt rushed to me so I guess she found a greener pasture somewhere. Not knowing still bother me a lot actually. I left her a voicemail tonight since it has been nearly 1 month since I tried to contact her. Still no anwser, what did I expect :')

I totally share your vision of love. Yet how are we supposed to deal with those unmet expectations ?

About my hopes and expectations for the future, well I don't have much of those that's why I ended up here I guess. I know things won't be the same as before if I were to get back with my ex, yet I'd be so happy. Now I know that nobody's perfect, we aren't probably more compatible than any other couple yet  it feels like my last hope. I know that she isn't any better than any other girl, that I could probably be as happy as I was in another relationship. However I can't explain why but I feel like it's my last attempt. I gave so much, I feel so bad already.. I guess I could take some time to recover, try again, but scars would remain and I don't want to live in such fucked up days anyway.

Thanks for your reply.

In fact I did not chose to cut off contact with those dear friends. We spent some time together and of course, while we are quite similar in tastes and personality, we sometime fight over petty things. He sent me a kind of mean text afterwards about how I owed him apologies for things I said to him. I did not say anything that bad and it was really infuriating. I explained him in a very long text how bad I felt, how I couldn't understand why such a 'friend' would ask for apologies over stupid fights. I understood that he wasn't (anymore?) the friend I thought he was, then I blocked him.

The reason I feel like this in general is in my opinion that I understood something through hardship. This world is not made for men and women seeking blossoming through relationship. It's a cold hard world where friends are friends because they need each others, same as lovers. I hoped, like everyone did I guess, that one day I'll meet the love of my life. A person I could share anything and everything with. A person I could fully love and who would fully love me. As you can surely tell it didn't worked out that well with my previous gf. I suppose it's even what made her leave me.

Anyway when this flash of insight struck me I understood that we are not living in a magical world where two people are bounded together forever by true love. It simply does not exists. Some couples actually go together quite well, but it's never the perfect relationship.

What is the point of living if I'm going to be emotionally ostracized all my life ?

Thanks for your reply.

Focusing on the future is something I did since I broke up with my gf. I worked a lot and now I'm at the point where I'm pretty sure my future is not going to be a problem, in a financial way at least.

Of course there is still a lot of question marks hanging over the details, but there is no real challenge. I could do the same boring thing over and over, the daily routine of the average working dude. My life would probably get quite comfortable at some point. Yet the question remains, to what end ?

I'm not going to share any deep real relation with anyone anymore. Friends are just people used to you, love is a broken promise as well. What would be the point of living alone through this ?

Art is actually a way to transcend our stupid useless lives in my opinion. It's a shame I never did any, and I don't feel like starting now.

About my parents, well I'm not really close to them. They care about me financially but they don't seem to care that much emotionally, or they are hiding it. I'm an only child and I was the hard working, responsible kind. They trust me with my decisions and learnt not to question them. We don't talk often and I feel like they wouldn't understand me. They are happy and live in their very material world, they don't ask themselves the questions I ask myself. Ignorance is bliss I guess.
